reason: The text extensively establishes the centrality of Yahweh to Hebrew identity. The Hebrews are repeatedly identified as 'the God of the Hebrews' (אֱלֹהֵ֣י הָֽעִבְרִ֔ים) throughout the narrative. The entire liberation effort is framed around their desire and right to worship and sacrifice to their God. Moses and Aaron consistently demand release so the people can serve (worship) Yahweh. The narrative demonstrates that Hebrew peoplehood is fundamentally bound to their relationship with and worship of Yahweh—their identity as a people is inseparable from their covenantal relationship to their God. The plagues themselves function to demonstrate Yahweh's power and establish His authority over them and Egypt, reinforcing that worship of Yahweh is central to what defines them as a distinct people.
